rows.description: A student picks engineering for job security and salary while secretly drawn to music; both sets of motives are real, and the tension shapes how much energy they bring.

rows.description: A parent notices a child now asks about the prize before every chore; the parent shifts toward noticing effort and meaning and uses rewards sparingly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: An adult stuck in a paid but joyless task looks for the part that connects to something they value or a skill they are building; meaning does not replace pay but can steady effort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child insists on putting on their own shoes even when it takes ages and they are late; the wish to act by their own will is strong and healthy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A parent lets a child choose between two study times or which subject first; small real choices increase cooperation because the child feels like an agent and not an object.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who is told every step of their day refuses even things they wanted to do; pushback often protects a threatened sense of ownership more than it rejects the task.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult who chooses a course after real reflection sustains effort through hardship better than one pushed into it; owned goals hold through setbacks.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A worker whose manager checks every step feels their energy drain and starts doing the minimum; without room for judgement, initiative fades, and clear outcomes with freedom in method restores it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child proudly ties a knot or jumps a step and asks to do it again and again; feeling able is a powerful engine for effort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child who fails repeatedly at fractions concludes they cannot do maths and stops trying; without experiences of getting better, motivation collapses.
